chunks: went to visit Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, but the permission to see him was delayed until he became distressed. Hisham had a gatekeeper who was wealthy in worldly goods but had no children. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) approached the gatekeeper and said: 'Is there something with you by which you could bring me to Hisham, and I will teach you a supplication by which you will have children?' He said: 'Yes.' So he brought him to Hisham and fulfilled all of his needs.

He said: When he had finished, the gatekeeper said to him: 'May I be your ransom! The supplication you mentioned to me?' He said to him: 'Yes — say each day, in the morning and the evening, "Glory be to God" seventy times, seek forgiveness ten times, glorify nine times, and conclude the tenth with seeking forgiveness. Then recite the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic:

"Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is Most Forgiving. He will send the sky upon you in abundance. And will aid you with wealth and sons, and will make for you gardens, and will make for you rivers." [Quran 71:10-12]
The gatekeeper recited it and was blessed with abundant offspring. And after that, he maintained connection with Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both).

Sulayman said: So I recited it too — I had married a cousin of mine and a child had been delayed from her — and I taught it to my wife and was blessed with a child. The woman claimed that whenever she desired to become pregnant, she would become pregnant when she recited it. And I taught it to more than one person among the Hashimites who had not been having children, and they were blessed with many children.

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A self-sacrificial formula of deep respect — 'May I be your ransom'
key_terms.حَاجِب: Chamberlain, gatekeeper, the officer responsible for controlling access to a caliph
key_terms.مِدْرَار: Continuously pouring, abundant rain — classical Quranic term for divine blessing
key_terms.وَفَدَ: Made a formal visit, traveled to meet (used for ambassadorial delegations)
key_terms.يُولَدُ لَكَ: Passive construction: 'children will be born for you', i.e., 'you will have children'

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Baqir teach for having children?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter between Imam al-Baqir (AS) and a gatekeeper of the Umayyad Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik. When denied prompt entry to Hisham's court, the Imam offered to teach the childless gatekeeper a supplication for fertility in exchange for admittance. The supplication involves glorifications, istighfar (seeking forgiveness), and the recitation of Quran 71:10-12 — the verses of Nuh in which God promises abundance, wealth, children, and rivers to those who persistently seek His forgiveness. The narrator Sulayman confirms its efficacy through personal testimony and corroboration from Hashimites who also received children after practicing it.
